title: Access and Expenditure Guardrails — Company-wide Procedures and Templates
author: Marina Lopez
content:
Overview

This page consolidates company-wide guardrails for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expense approvals, vendor lifecycle controls, and travel spending. It provides: a one-page approval matrix, step-by-step procedures, role ownership, and ready-to-use templates for common workflows. Use this as the canonical reference for cross-functional requests and for onboarding new managers who approve spend or grant access.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Reduce operational friction while preserving least-privilege, cost discipline, and compliance.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and temporary vendors that interact with Redwood systems, finance, or data stores. Exemptions require written approval from finance-legal and security.

1) Access & Permissions
Summary: All access must follow least-privilege principles, time-bound access for non-permanent needs, and documented approvals in the access ticket.

Key roles
- Requester: Person who needs access.
- Manager approver: Requester’s direct manager or project owner.
- System owner: The team that operates the target service (e.g., eng-infra, data-team).
- Security reviewer: Required for privileged roles and cross-organization data access.

Standard process (short):
1. Requester files an Access Request using the Access Request template (ID: TPL-ACCESS-01).
2. Manager approves in the ticketing system (Jira).
3. System owner confirms role mapping and grants time-bound access (default expiry 30 days).
4. If role is privileged (see Privileged Role List), Security must also approve.

Privileged roles and exceptions
- Privileged roles include: infra-admin, db-admin, k8s-cluster-admin, hsm-admin.
- Any cross-environment data access (prod -> non-prod sync or vice versa) requires a data-justification attachment and security approval.

Example CLI snippet the infra team may use for time-bound grants:
- rbacctl grant --user jane@redwood.com --role db-readonly --resource prod-cluster --expiry 30d --ticket REDWOOD-1234

Audit and attestations
- Quarterly attestation: Owners must validate active memberships for privileged groups every quarter.
- Ad-hoc audit triggers: A sensitive data incident automatically triggers a membership snapshot and review for all accounts with access.

2) Change Management (service, infra, and config changes)
Principles: Small, reversible changes; staged rollouts; automated safety checks; and clear rollback plans.

Change categories and approval thresholds
| Category | Risk band | Approval required | Typical lead time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Configuration change (non-prod) | Low | Team owner | 24–48h |
| Infra change (prod, non-disruptive) | Medium | Team owner + SRE oncall | 48–72h |
| Schema changes (prod DB) | High | Team owner + SRE + DB steward + Change board | 7–14 days |
| Software release with DB migration | Critical | Change board + Product + Security + Exec sponsor | 14+ days |

Standard workflow (numbered):
1. Create a Change Request (CR) using the CR template (TPL-CHANGE-02). Include risk assessment, test plan, and rollback steps.
2. Run automated preflight tests in staging.
3. Post results to the CR; notify SRE and product stakeholders.
4. Obtain required approvals according to the table above.
5. Schedule a deployment window with SRE and execute canary first.
6. Monitor metrics for 30 minutes (or the business-defined period).
7. If metrics breach thresholds, execute rollback and run post-incident review.

Change board and emergency changes
- Change board meets weekly and consists of representatives from Eng-Platform, Eng-SRE, Security, and Product.
- Emergency changes: Document emergency justification in the ticket and obtain retroactive approvals within 24 hours of the change.

3) Data Management and Classification
Data classification levels
- Public: Information intentionally shared externally. No special handling required.
- Internal: Business working data. Access on a need-to-know basis.
- Confidential: Customer data, PII, or intellectual property. Encryption at rest & transit required.
- Restricted: Legal, HR employee records, or regulated data (PCI, PHI equivalents). Multi-owner approval and stricter retention.

Handling rules by class (short table)
| Class | Encryption | Backups | Retention | Access pattern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Optional | Optional | 1 year recommended | Wide read access |
| Internal | In transit | Regular | 2 years | Need-to-know |
| Confidential | AES-256 at rest | Encrypted backups | 7 years or contractual | Manager + Security approval |
| Restricted | HSM-backed keys | Separated retention | Per law/contract | Security + Legal approval |

Retention & deletion procedure (numbered):
1. Identify data owner and classification tag.
2. Verify retention requirements from Legal or contract.
3. Submit Data Deletion Request (TPL-DATA-DEL-01) for records beyond retention.
4. System owner executes deletion and records proof (hash + timestamp).

Data access example: cross-team analytics requiring customer-level identifiers must include a redaction plan or tokenization step; if not feasible, request a Confidential data access review.

4) Procurement & Expense Approvals
Goal: Ensure predictable spend, consistency of vendor selection, and controls for fraud and duplicate payments.

Expense approval matrix
| Expense type | Amount | Approver | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Employee reimbursable expense | <= $250 | Manager | Use travel card where available |
| Employee reimbursable expense | $251–$2,500 | Manager + Finance reviewer | Receipts required |
| Capital equipment | $2,501–$25,000 | Manager + Finance | PO required |
| Strategic procurement | > $25,000 | Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor | RFP or formal vendor review |

Procurement workflow (short):
1. Raise Purchase Requisition (PR) in procurement tool with justification and GL code.
2. For purchases > $2,500 attach vendor W-9 (or equivalent) and conflict-of-interest statement.
3. Finance validates budget; Legal validates contract terms for > $25k.
4. Finance issues PO; vendor only invoices against PO.

Corporate card and travel card rules
- Use corporate card for travel and approved vendor spend.
- Cardholders are expected to submit receipts within 7 calendar days of transaction.
- Suspicious charges trigger an automated cardhold pending review.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
Objective: Reduce supply risk, ensure contractual protections, and maintain a single vendor record per legal entity.

Minimum onboarding artifacts
- Completed Vendor Intake Form (TPL-VENDOR-01).
- Signed Master Services Agreement (MSA) or PO-based terms.
- Security attestation: SOC2 or vendor security questionnaire (for vendors touching data).
- Insurance certificates where applicable.

Onboarding steps (numbered):
1. Procurement raises vendor intake and assigns a vendor owner.
2. Legal prepares or reviews MSA; Finance opens vendor profile (w-9/equivalent).
3. Security runs an initial risk assessment for vendors with system/network access.
4. Approve, sign, and store contract in the contract repository.
5. Assign vendor SLAs and monitoring points.

Vendor renewals and offboarding
- Annual renewal: Confirm scope, pricing, and security posture.
- Offboarding checklist: revoke accounts, reclaim secrets, and confirm final invoice. Use TPL-VENDOR-OFFBOARD-02.

6) Travel and Business Expenses
Principles: Reasonable, cost-conscious, and aligned with the business purpose.

Travel booking rules
- Book lowest reasonable fare; prefer refundable fares when travel schedule is uncertain.
- Use company travel vendors where available for preferred rates.
- Mileage reimbursement follows the published IRS-equivalent rate.

Per diems and meals
- Domestic day travel meal cap: $80/day.
- International per diem: location-specific — refer to the travel rates spreadsheet (link in templates).

Approvals and exceptions
- Manager approves travel. For travel > $5,000 or with international regulatory implications, obtain Finance approval.
- Exceptions (e.g., last-minute upgrades) require pre-approval or post-facto justification.

Expense submission checklist
1. Submit expense report within 14 days of travel end date.
2. Attach itemized receipts and the related meeting justification.
3. Tag report with GL code and project ID.

7) Templates, Forms, and Quick Links
This section lists the canonical templates referenced above and where to find them in the templates repo.
- TPL-ACCESS-01 — Access Request form (fields: requester, role, justification, expiry, ticket).
- TPL-CHANGE-02 — Change Request template (fields: risk, rollback, test plan).
- TPL-DATA-DEL-01 — Data Deletion Request.
- TPL-VENDOR-01 — Vendor Intake Form.
- TPL-VENDOR-OFFBOARD-02 — Vendor Offboarding checklist.
- TPL-PR-01 — Purchase Requisition template (includes required approvals and GL codes).

8) Ownership, Escalation, and Contacts
Primary owners
- Finance (procurement, spend controls): Director of Finance.
- Legal (contracts, exceptions): Head of Legal.
- Security (access models, privileged approvals): Security Engineering Manager.
- People Ops (travel policy, employee-facing templates): People Ops Lead.

Escalation path (short):
1. If a manager is unavailable, route approvals to the manager’s designated delegate.
2. For conflicts between teams (budget vs. security), escalate to the cross-functional Change Board.
3. For suspected fraud or security incidents, pause related approvals and notify Security and Legal immediately.

9) Monitoring, KPIs, and Continuous Improvement
Suggested KPIs to track
- Mean time to grant access (target: < 2 business days for non-privileged).
- Percentage of expenses submitted within SLA (target: > 90%).
- Vendor renewal risk score distribution.
- Number of emergency changes with retroactive approvals (target: reduction YoY).

Continuous improvement cadence
- Quarterly review of approval thresholds by Finance and People Ops.
- Annual tabletop exercise for vendor compromise and offboarding.
- Semi-annual review of templates and ticket fields for clarity.

Appendix A — Quick decision tables and IDs
- Expense template ID: TPL-PR-01
- Access template: TPL-ACCESS-01
- Change request: TPL-CHANGE-02
- Vendor intake: TPL-VENDOR-01

Appendix B — Example approval email snippet (copy/paste)
Subject: Approval request — RED-REQ-1234 (Purchase: Cloud GPU seats)
Body:
Manager,
Please approve the attached Purchase Requisition (PR-9876) for 10 GPU seats for Q1. Total spend: $18,500. Budget: ENG-Q1-2025. Vendor: CloudCompute Co.
Approvers needed: Manager, Finance.
Rationale: Temporary capacity for model benchmarking tied to roadmap milestone.
Thanks,
Requester name

If you need a clarification, or to request an exception to any of the controls in this guide, open an exception request via the Exception Request form (TPL-EXC-01) and assign it to Finance-Legal and Security for review.
